units.function: Paperclip's instance-level Adapter management page: list built-in/external runtime modules, install from npm or local paths, hide or pause overrides, hot-reload, reinstall latest and destructively remove stored packages.
units.dependencyDirection: A single 692-line React page depends on instance-global Adapter APIs, company context only for navigation, dynamic UI parser/schema caches, direct npm-registry fetches and host-path selection. It mixes supply-chain operations, effective-runtime projection and presentation without a domain-level Connector contract.
units.keyDataModels: AdapterInfo type/source/package/version/model count/loaded/disabled/capabilities, built-in override precedence, optional install version/local-path mode, mutation state, reinstall target and client-synthesized virtual built-in rows.
units.lifecycle: List effective adapters; install arbitrary npm/local code; optionally override a built-in type; hide or pause; hot-reload and invalidate client parser/schema caches; reinstall npm latest; remove registration and package files from disk.
units.testAssessment: No dedicated focused test was found by repository/symbol search; App routing and the component inventory reference the page. Existing TypeScript was verified with `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p ui/tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false` on 2026-08-19. The normal pnpm-filter typecheck did not run because pnpm requested an interactive modules-directory purge, and the read-only audit did not permit dependency mutation. No behavior test proves authorization, supply-chain verification, rollback, active-run draining, accessibility/mobile flows or failure recovery.
units.designRationale: Provide a lightweight runtime-extension mechanism simpler than plugins: a package exports createServerAdapter(), registers model discovery/execution and can override or extend built-ins without restarting the whole application.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral Connector administration with explicit capabilities, identity binding, health, runtime attestation, version pinning, secret/data boundaries, approval pause/resume, staged rollout, rollback and managed-cloud versus self-hosted policy—not arbitrary instance-global module hot-swaps.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT in Company OS Web over a versioned ConnectorCatalog/Deployment API. Adapt only source/version/override visibility and separate installed-versus-effective inventory. Installation must be server-governed, pinned by digest, license/provenance scanned, sandboxed or externally isolated, policy-approved and deployed through compatibility test, canary, drain and rollback states. Do not copy the page or its ServerAdapterModule assumptions.
units.responsibilityConflict: Installing, globally replacing, hot-swapping or deleting execution code affects every dependent Agent yet requires no accountable human, purpose, impact set, risk classification, approval digest or immutable receipt. Existing Agents silently use a new latest version on the next run, and destructive removal has no dependency/rebinding or execution-drain workflow.

securityFindings: The UI permits installing arbitrary npm packages or host filesystem paths as executable server modules without displaying signature, digest, publisher trust, license, sandbox, requested permissions or data-egress impact.

Optional version input and reinstall-latest make deployments non-reproducible; hot-swap affects existing Agents on their next run without per-Agent version binding, compatibility proof, canary or rollback.
Latest-version lookup is a direct browser request to the public npm registry, leaks package-use metadata, fails offline and silently reduces errors to unavailable.
Local-path installation exposes a host filesystem/code-execution boundary and accepts cross-platform paths without visible allowlist, canonicalization, ownership or deployment-profile constraints.
Instance-global APIs are shown under company-derived navigation, which can obscure tenant/instance authority and impact scope.

Hide, override-pause and loaded/effective semantics are overloaded; the client synthesizes virtual built-in rows with loaded=true, zero models and empty capabilities, so inventory/health truth is lossy.
Reload/reinstall invalidate only browser parser/schema caches; no visible distributed cache/version fencing, active-run drain or Connector attestation prevents mixed-version execution.
Destructive removal deletes stored packages and cannot be undone, but shows no dependent Agents/runs, migration target, package retention, rollback artifact or approval evidence.
Mutation errors are raw strings and operations lack stable action/job codes, durable status, cancellation and operator-visible recovery.
The page has no dedicated behavioral tests despite controlling executable supply-chain and destructive lifecycle operations.
